meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone hear Owen first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it, or after?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. A paste means he drafted it somewhere else, nothing more. Show me that screen, Hale.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. And you still haven't said whether Owen was heard before the zero.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Seventeen-year-olds get quotations wrong every day, Hale. That's a citation error, not a zero.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
An outline is a first guess; students change their minds two weeks later, that's the point of one.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So he was heard, a day before you entered it. A boy put on the spot by his teacher freezes. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and nobody in that class hears a word of it.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against an essay written at home with time to fix the commas. That isn't a comparison. What exactly are you proposing?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because your own procedure says it can't carry anything on its own. I asked what you're proposing.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

Fine, to put this behind him: the rewrite, supervised, private, nowhere near his classmates, and marked before December 1. Nothing on his record, and I want all of that from you in writing tonight. Owen didn't do anything, and nobody will hear it that way.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Yes, once your email says so tonight and the mark is in before December 1.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, after school. Put the day and the room in tonight's email. Ten minutes.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
And Thursday after school, marked well before December 1. Then yes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Just the email, tonight, with everything we said in it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday after school, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require all of this in writing, including the day and room, with the new mark entered before December 1. I expect your email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school that replaces the zero with nothing on file, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight and the mark entered before December 1; that is the fair outcome, procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her call.
What moved her: Laying out the version history with its exact times and offering to pull it up for her, because it was dated, tied to Owen's own file, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Leaving her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero unanswered for several turns, because she had to keep pressing it instead of engaging with your evidence.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay in one late-night window on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was heard, answer right away with your November 2 conversation before moving to the version history.
